quests.title: Find a pattern that repeats in an unexpected place
quests.description: Look for a visual rhythm or repeating motif somewhere you wouldn't expect to find one. It might be a grid, a texture, or a shape that recurs.
tips: Check drainage grates, fences, brickwork, or pavement tiles
Look up at window arrangements or balcony railings
Notice shadows cast by repeating structures

quests.title: Count the different materials on a single door
quests.description: A door is rarely made of one thing. Find a door and identify every material you can see — wood, metal, glass, rubber, paint, fabric.
tips: Include hinges, handles, frames, and weatherstripping
Note where different materials meet
Look for materials that have aged differently

quests.title: Find three different textures on one ordinary wall
quests.description: Walls are rarely uniform. Find one wall that shows at least three distinct surface qualities — rough concrete, smooth plaster, paint, brick, tile, weathering.
tips: Repairs often create texture contrasts
Notice where the light catches different surfaces differently
Look for where materials meet at an edge

quests.title: Spot a color gradient in the built environment
quests.description: Find a surface or structure where color visibly changes from one area to another — rust fading into metal, bleached paint, water staining, or moss growth.
tips: Sun exposure and moisture create natural gradients
Look at large concrete surfaces at an angle
Old brick walls often show color variation by height

quests.title: Find evidence of a building that used to be here
quests.description: Look for ghost signs, filled-in doorways, different-colored brick patches, or foundation marks that reveal something was once attached to or built here.
tips: Look for outline marks on walls where rooflines once met
Notice different brick colors or stone patches
Look for sealed-off windows or doors at odd heights

quests.title: Find a sign that has outlived its purpose
quests.description: Ghost signs, painted-over lettering, or faded advertisements from businesses that no longer exist. What can you still read?
tips: High brick walls often preserve faded painted ads
Look for embossed or cast lettering on metal fixtures
Notice text on glass that's been partially scraped off

quests.title: Find a surface that shows multiple layers of repair
quests.description: Infrastructure repairs leave visible archaeological layers — patches over patches, different generations of paint, concrete poured at different times.
tips: Pavements often show circular patches from utility work
Walls show rectangular patches where damage was fixed
Look for different shades of the same material

quests.title: Find a place where two different eras of construction meet
quests.description: Where an old building was extended, or a new structure built against an old one. Notice how the materials and styles change at the joint.
tips: Look for visible seam lines in brickwork or stonework
Notice changes in window style or proportion
Different foundation levels are sometimes visible

quests.title: Find a design decision that makes your life easier without you noticing
quests.description: Good design is often invisible. Find a small feature — a beveled edge, a drainage channel, a non-slip surface — that solves a problem silently.
tips: Look at curb cuts, tactile paving, and handrail endings
Notice how street furniture is positioned relative to foot traffic
Check where drainage goes on sloped surfaces

quests.title: Find a design decision that makes someone's life harder
quests.description: Bad design is everywhere — a bench with dividers to prevent lying down, a door that pushes when you expect to pull, a step where a ramp should be.
tips: Notice where people have created informal paths around official routes
Look for wear patterns showing where people actually walk
Check where pavement edges are difficult for wheels

quests.title: Find a utility object that was clearly designed with care
quests.description: A drain cover, a lamp post, a bench, a postbox — something functional that someone also tried to make beautiful or elegant.
tips: Historic cast iron features often have decorative elements
Look at how simple shapes are refined — rounded edges, tapering forms
Notice proportions: is this object satisfying to look at?

quests.title: Find evidence of how people actually use a space versus how it was designed
quests.description: Worn grass paths, improvised seats, moved barriers, scratched surfaces — how has real use changed or contradicted the designer's intention?
tips: Look for 'desire paths' where people cross grass or avoid official routes
Notice what's been added informally — bags, bikes, notices
Check where surfaces are worn or polished differently

quests.title: Find a shadow that reveals something invisible in direct light
quests.description: Shadows cast by structures, vegetation, or objects sometimes make detail visible that disappears in full light — texture, lettering, form.
tips: Early morning and late afternoon light cast long revealing shadows
Look at text or relief carved into stone or metal
Notice how rough surfaces show more texture in raking light

quests.title: Find a place where light bounces unexpectedly
quests.description: Reflected light from windows, puddles, polished metal, or pale surfaces can illuminate areas that seem to have no direct light source.
tips: Look at shadowed faces of buildings near reflective surfaces
Notice colored light from stained glass or colored awnings
Puddles reflect a different view of the sky or buildings

quests.title: Find a texture that changes dramatically when viewed in different light
quests.description: Some surfaces look flat in overcast light but reveal deep texture in direct sun. Find one and notice exactly how the light changes what you see.
tips: Concrete, stone, and aged wood respond dramatically to light angle
Look at the same surface from multiple positions
Notice the difference between the lit and shadowed side

quests.title: Find a shadow that creates an interesting shape separate from its source
quests.description: Sometimes a shadow has a clearer or more interesting form than the object casting it — a bicycle shadow, tree shadow pattern, or architectural detail.
tips: Fence shadows create geometric patterns on ground
Plant shadows are often more complex than the plants themselves
Look at how shadow edges change with surface texture

quests.title: Find a right angle that isn't quite right
quests.description: Settling, subsidence, and age cause corners to shift. Find a corner, frame, or edge that appears to be a right angle but has drifted slightly.
tips: Old buildings often have corners that have settled unevenly
Look at door frames — gaps and wedges reveal movement
Cracked plaster or tile often reveals structural geometry

quests.title: Find a circle in a world of rectangles
quests.description: Urban environments are dominated by right angles. Find a functional circular element — a drain, a pipe section, a dome, a wheel — and look closely at how it meets the rectangular world around it.
tips: Look at how circular pipes fit through rectangular walls
Notice how round columns meet square floors
Drain covers create circles in pavement grids

quests.title: Find a vertical line that becomes horizontal
quests.description: Pipes, cables, rails, or edges that start vertical and curve or transition to horizontal. Trace the line and notice how the transition is handled.
tips: Downpipes transition from vertical to horizontal at the ground
Handrails curve at their ends
Roof edges create the junction of vertical wall and horizontal sky

quests.title: Find a structure that appears to be unsupported
quests.description: A cantilevered overhang, a floating step, a bridge section, a shelf — something that seems to defy gravity. How does it actually work?
tips: Balconies often cantilever from a building's structure
Signs and awnings are attached at fewer points than they seem
Bridge sections are sometimes suspended rather than supported
